traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Gymnosperms (DELTA, 2008 onwards, version of 5 August 2019), Cupressaceae and Taxodiaceae (Taxodiaceae now in Cupressaceae, as the Library has it): mature leaves mostly small, scale-like and single-veined, sometimes linear like the juvenile ones, in Juniperus needle-like or both on one plant; in Cupressaceae opposite and decussate or in whorls of three or four, in Taxodiaceae mostly spiral (alternate) and opposite only in Metasequoia; monoecious or dioecious, junipers usually dioecious. Taxodiaceae's spiral leaves are the rare state, as the redwoods and swamp cypresses are few beside the cypresses and junipers.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 153, 155, 156, family Cupressaceae: leaf habit evergreen, usually; read as {"evergreen": "usually"}.
